reasoning_traces.think:
The Kelly criterion is derived from maximizing expected logarithmic utility, U(F,p) = p·log(1+F) + q·log(1-F). This utility function defines a zero-crossing F* such that U(F*,p) = 0, separating submartingale (growth) and supermartingale (decay) regimes. The sign of U(F,p) determines whether a bet fraction leads to average wealth growth or decay. The variance estimate VAR(W(N)) ≈ 2·|W(0)|²·N·p(1-p)·F² shows how risk scales with bet size, enabling risk-adjusted sizing. Fractional Kelly F̄_K = f·F_K introduces a safety margin, reducing exposure when edge is uncertain. These primitives form a coherent framework for sizing and regime classification in stochastic binary games.
